title: 2 Samuel 18
paragraphs: ¹ David mustered the men who were with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds. ² David sent out his troops, a third under the command of Joab, a third under Joab's brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. The king told the troops, “I myself will surely march out with you.” ³ But the men said, “You must not go out; if we are forced to flee, they won't care about us. Even if half of us die, they won't care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It would be better now for you to give us support from the city.” ⁴ The king answered, “I will do whatever seems best to you.” So the king stood beside the gate while all his men marched out in units of hundreds and of thousands. ⁵ The king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Be gentle with the young man Absalom for my sake.” And all the troops heard the king's command to each of the commanders about Absalom.

⁶ So the army went out into the field against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim. ⁷ There Israel’s troops were routed by David’s men, and the casualties that day were great—twenty thousand men. ⁸ The battle spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest swallowed up more men that day than the sword.

¹¹ Joab said to the man who had told him, "You saw him — why didn't you strike him down on the spot? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a belt." ¹² But the man replied, "Even if you had put a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I would not have raised a hand against the king's son. We all heard the king order you and Abishai and Ittai, 'Protect the young man Absalom.' ¹³ If I had done it, I would have been risking my own life — nothing is hidden from the king, and you yourself would have turned against me." ¹⁴ Joab said, "I'm not going to waste time arguing with you." He took three spears in his hand and drove them into Absalom's chest while he was still alive, hanging in the oak tree. ¹⁵ Then ten of Joab's armor-bearers surrounded Absalom and finished him off.

¹⁶ Joab sounded the trumpet, and the troops stopped pursuing Israel, for Joab called them back. ¹⁷ They took Absalom, threw him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge heap of stones over him. All Israel fled to their own homes. ¹⁸ During his lifetime, Absalom had set up a stone pillar for himself in the King's Valley, for he had said, "I have no son to carry on the memory of my name." He named the pillar after himself, and it is still called Absalom's Monument to this day. ¹⁹ Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and bring the news to the king that the LORD has vindicated him against his enemies." ²⁰ But Joab told him, "You're not the one to bring news today. You can bring news another time, but not today — the king's son is dead."

²¹ Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed to Joab and ran off. ²² But Ahimaaz son of Zadok pressed Joab again: "Whatever happens, please let me run after the Cushite." Joab said, "Why do you want to run, my son? You have no news that will bring you a reward." ²³ "No matter," he said, "let me run." So Joab said, "Run." Ahimaaz took the route through the plain and outran the Cushite. ²⁴ David was sitting between the inner and outer gates. The watchman had gone up to the roof of the gateway by the wall. He looked out and saw a man running alone. ²⁵ The watchman called down and told the king. The king said, "If he's alone, he must be bringing news." He kept coming, drawing nearer.

²⁶ The watchman saw another man running and called out to the gatekeeper, "Look — another man running alone!" The king said, "He's bringing news too." ²⁷ The watchman said, "The first man runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." "He's a good man," said the king. "He comes with good news." ²⁸ Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well!" He bowed down before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Praise the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who lifted their hands against my lord the king." ²⁹ "Is the young man Absalom safe?" the king asked. Ahimaaz answered, "I saw a great commotion just as Joab was sending the king's servant and me, your servant, but I didn't know what it was." ³⁰ The king said, "Step aside and wait here." So he stepped aside and stood there.

³¹ Then the Cushite arrived and said, "Good news, my lord the king! The LORD has vindicated you today against all who rose up against you." ³² The king asked the Cushite, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" The Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise against you to harm you end up like that young man." ³³ The king was shaken. He went up to the room over the gateway and wept. As he went, he cried out, "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you — O Absalom, my son, my son!"
